findings.reason: the plan must name `TRANSCRIPT_ROOT` and have the census reuse it (or take the root as a parameter fed from it), rather than fork the root a fourth time.
findings.text: §2 says the census enumerates transcripts "through `transcript_index` in `reckon/velocity.py`, the owner of locating Claude Code transcripts", but `transcript_index(root)` (`reckon/velocity.py:1363`) takes a root it does not resolve; the root is the constant `TRANSCRIPT_ROOT = Path.home() / ".claude" / "projects"` at `reckon/velocity.py:81`, consumed at the caller `reckon/velocity.py:1674` (`transcript_index(transcript_root)`), so a census that resolves `~/.claude/projects` itself becomes a second owner of it

findings.reason: the shared helper must own the component test for every caller (coordinator obligations and the worker fence included) and §2 must state which classification wins for the legacy temp pool, or the census drifts from the owners it is meant to extend and misclassifies a reaped temp-pool worktree as temporary.
findings.text: §2 claims the worktree-root component test "moves into one helper in `reckon/crew/routing.py`, which `_workspace_roots` and the census both call", but the same convention is spelled independently by `_WORKTREE_COMPONENT = ".reckon-worktrees"` at `reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:239` (used by `_repository_named_by_worktree`, which reads the component under `.reckon-worktrees` from a path exactly as the census helper must) and by `root / "Code" / ".reckon-worktrees"` at `reckon/_worker_fence.py:780`; the extracted predicate in `_workspace_roots` is `sum(part.lstrip(".") == "reckon-worktrees" for part in preferred.parts) > 1` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:464`), a *root* nesting guard, not the `>= 1` membership test an arbitrary candidate path needs; and the legacy pool is `tempfile.gettempdir() / "reckon-worktrees" / stem` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:469`), so a reaped worktree under it satisfies both §2's "sits under a `reckon-worktrees` root" and "under the system temporary directory" rules with no stated precedence

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one module `reckon/mcp_census.py` hides the MCP-log walk, the failure-signature pattern table, the working-directory classification and the transcript walk behind a single `census(start, end)` function called by the doctor block and by a direct caller.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the census re-resolves the transcript root, and the worktree-root convention keeps owners these units do not consolidate.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1613, cli_options 336, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2 adds to the `public_definitions` family (the module `reckon/mcp_census.py` and its `census` function) and states in its own text why nothing is retired ("no existing reader counts MCP connections or storage-slow results"), and that it adds no command and no option.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §2 cites the mechanisms it extends (`_in_linked_worktree` at `reckon/cli_entry.py:132`, `_workspace_roots` at `reckon/crew/routing.py:454`, and `transcript_index`/`promotion_receipts`/`TRANSCRIPT_ROOT` in `reckon/velocity.py`), and no reader of the Claude Code MCP logs or of `storage-slow` counts exists to reuse (grep for `mcp-logs`/`claude-cli-nodejs` finds nothing; `storage-slow` appears only as the producer constant `STORAGE_SLOW` in `reckon/_mcp_tools.py:9` and its consumers in `reckon/mcp.py`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two helpers §2 extracts (the worktree-root component test in `reckon/crew/routing.py` and the content-block walk in `reckon/velocity.py`) are de-duplications of loops the owners already run inline, not new layers placed beside them, and `promotion_receipts` keeps its behaviour under its existing tests.
